segment: merchant Bitcoin jobs beyond conventional POS

scope.purpose: Atomic merchant requirements derived from Bitcoin protocol and selected official implementation documentation, as a standalone native acceptance design input; this is a separate-origin requirements bundle, not a competitor parity claim.
scope.basis: Research/planning only. Protocol capabilities and documented mechanics identify merchant jobs, risks, candidate improvements, measurable proof, and limits. They do not establish OpenBMT implementation or compatibility.
product_boundaries: Follow docs/research/standalone-pos-delivery-plan-2026-11-16.md: merchant-controlled on-chain receiving; Lightning separate and gated by capacity, funding, availability and recovery.

Preserve local hot start or independently created cold wallet, public-only pairing, verification on wallet display, owner-approved transfer, issued-address/late-payment tracking, and independent recovery.
Do not alter current signing behavior, imply hard maximum-loss guarantee, require custody or fiat conversion, add settlement network, or imply provider permission for recovery.
Distinguish key ownership from live Lightning channel-state independence; never describe liquidity as free or prepaid without evidence.
No code, implementation, tests/builds, accounts, network mutations, or third-party contact were performed.
scope.evidence_limit: Sources are official protocol specifications, official software documentation, or an official device-format source. Functional paraphrases only. Documentation is not tested compatibility; unknowns are retained.

sources.title: BIP 321: URI Scheme
sources.qualifiers: Bitcoin BIPs repository; current page inspected 2026-11-17.
sources.evidence_note: BIP proposes modern Bitcoin payment instruction URIs; receiving software still requires user authorization. Replaces/supersedes BIP 21 context.

sources.title: BIP 32: Hierarchical Deterministic Wallets
sources.qualifiers: Bitcoin BIPs repository; current page inspected 2026-11-17.
sources.evidence_note: HD wallet trees permit sharing public derivation capability without sharing spending private keys, but do not themselves define all wallet policies or operational security.

sources.title: Bitcoin Core: Mempool Replacements
sources.qualifiers: Bitcoin Core repository; current policy document inspected 2026-11-17; local node policy may differ.
sources.evidence_note: Mempool replacement behavior is relay policy, separate from consensus confirmation; a seen transaction can be replaced subject to node policy.

sources.title: Bitcoin Core wallet spend RPC
sources.qualifiers: Bitcoin Core master source inspected 2026-11-17; option details may change between releases.
sources.evidence_note: Wallet spending exposes fee rate and confirmation target choices, demonstrating fee and timing tradeoffs; this is a software interface reference, not a claim about merchant receive requirements.

sources.title: BOLT 2: Peer Protocol for Channel Management
sources.qualifiers: Lightning BOLTs repository current master inspected 2026-11-17; implementation/version-dependent.
sources.evidence_note: Lightning channels have evolving protocol state, coordinated updates, and cooperative or unilateral closing behavior; stale or lost state is safety critical.

sources.title: BOLT 3: Bitcoin Transaction and Script Formats
sources.qualifiers: Lightning BOLTs repository current master inspected 2026-11-17.
sources.evidence_note: Lightning channels are funded by on-chain transactions and rely on commitment transaction scripts and timelocks.

sources.title: BOLT 5: Recommendations for On-chain Transaction Handling
sources.qualifiers: Lightning BOLTs repository current master inspected 2026-11-17.
sources.evidence_note: Channel failure can require on-chain handling and output sweeping; resolution is not equivalent to immediate wallet availability.

sources.title: BOLT 7: P2P Node and Channel Discovery
sources.qualifiers: Lightning BOLTs repository current master inspected 2026-11-17; public routing data is not a route guarantee.
sources.evidence_note: Routing view is derived from distributed announcements and updates; announced channels need confirmation depth and advertised fee/expiry parameters.

sources.title: BOLT 11: Invoice Protocol for Lightning Payments
sources.section: Encoding, amount, QR codes, payer/payee requirements
sources.qualifiers: Lightning BOLTs repository current master inspected 2026-11-17.
sources.evidence_note: Invoices encode payment requests in a QR-friendly format; amount may be absent, and invoice validity and payment are separate operations.

sources.title: BOLT 4: Onion Routing Protocol
sources.qualifiers: Lightning BOLTs repository current master inspected 2026-11-17.
sources.evidence_note: Lightning payments traverse hops using conditional payments and may fail with encrypted routing errors; failure is a normal operational case.

sources.title: LDK rust-lightning 0.2.8 source package
sources.section: src/ln/channelmanager.rs: ChannelManager vs ChannelMonitor; initialization and persistence
sources.qualifiers: Cargo.lock pins lightning 0.2.8; matching published crate source inspected locally at .cargo/registry/src/index.crates.io-1949cf8c6b5b557f/lightning-0.2.8/src/ln/channelmanager.rs. docs.rs page was not remotely verified.
sources.evidence_note: The source distinguishes off-chain ChannelManager state from on-chain ChannelMonitor enforcement and requires persisted monitors and chain catch-up during restart. This is LDK library behavior, not product deployment proof.

sources.title: LND: Recovery
sources.qualifiers: Lightning Labs LND official repository current master inspected 2026-11-17; LND-specific comparator, not generic guarantee.
sources.evidence_note: LND recovery describes channel backup restoration as a recovery path involving peers and channel closure, not restoration of a live identical channel state.

sources.title: NFC Forum: Introduction to NFC Forum Tags
sources.qualifiers: NFC Forum document inspected 2026-11-17; device/app interoperability remains to be tested.
sources.evidence_note: NDEF can encode URI records; this source establishes a carrier format, not that a phone opens a payment app or that a Bitcoin payment URI will work cross-device.

sources.title: BIP 125: Opt-in Full Replace-by-Fee Signaling
sources.qualifiers: Bitcoin BIPs repository inspected 2026-11-17; use Core current policy source for current behavior.
sources.evidence_note: Recipients may defer treating an unconfirmed replaceable transaction as payment; BIP 125 is policy background and current node policies may differ.

sources.title: Bitcoin Core walletcreatefundedpsbt RPC
sources.section: feeRate, lockUnspents, selected inputs and change outputs
sources.qualifiers: Bitcoin Core 24.0.0 official RPC reference; feature details are version-specific and this is a narrow wallet comparator.
sources.evidence_note: Wallet RPC exposes fee-rate selection and optional locking of selected unspent outputs, supporting explicit review and reservation requirements.

sources.title: Bitcoin Core wallet data model
sources.qualifiers: Bitcoin Core current master source inspected 2026-11-17; not a universal wallet mandate.
sources.evidence_note: Wallet source describes avoid_reuse as a privacy measure to avoid creating transactions that spend from the same addresses.

claims.capability: Receive to merchant-controlled keys
claims.merchant_outcome: Funds are received to keys the merchant controls and can recover independently.
claims.behavior: Choose local hot start or independently created cold wallet; pair public-only receive information; verify each displayed address on the wallet’s own trusted display.
claims.preconditions: Compatible wallet backup and address derivation are configured.
claims.qualifiers: Existing plan accepts these authority modes; current signing behavior is unchanged; no custody or company recovery authority is added.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: Lost checkout device must not lose merchant spending authority; recovery procedure is documented and independently exercised.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Make authority state and the exact public descriptor/address derivation visible, with a recovery artifact check before accepting funds.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Merchant key control can remove dependence on an account provider to authorize receipt or recovery; prove by restore without a company service.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Self-custody shifts key protection and recovery burden to the merchant; public-only pairing does not guarantee recovery by itself.
claims.acceptance_test: Recover a test wallet from its merchant-held backup on a clean device and verify derived address matches; no private key is exposed during pairing.

claims.capability: Use distinct receiving addresses and keep old requests trackable
claims.merchant_outcome: The merchant can reconcile each incoming payment to the correct sale while reducing address reuse.
claims.behavior: Issue a fresh address for each request and retain the mapping to sale, derivation index, issue time, expiry policy, and status.
claims.preconditions: Wallet can derive addresses and durable journal stores mappings.
claims.qualifiers: BIP32 supports public derivation; the requirement is merchant workflow, not proof of wallet behavior.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: On restart or wallet migration, restore issued-address mappings so late transactions still match.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Persist issued addresses and status independently from device-local UI state; expose restore coverage.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: One-time addresses are compatible with self-controlled derivation and local records; measure correct association across restart and restore.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: More addresses increase tracking and backup requirements; address uniqueness does not make transactions anonymous.
claims.acceptance_test: Issue 100 requests, restart and restore from backup, then reconcile payments to original sales including an expired request.

claims.capability: Observe receiving without spend authority
claims.merchant_outcome: A checkout device can display and monitor receiving requests without holding spending keys.
claims.behavior: Import only public derivation material and verify a test address against the cold wallet display; reject secret-bearing pairing payloads.
claims.preconditions: Cold wallet exposes compatible public data and merchant verifies on independent screen.
claims.qualifiers: Does not alter current signing behavior; an xpub may still disclose privacy-sensitive derivation data.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: If watch-only data is lost, restore from owner-held public backup; spending remains on independently held signer.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Show authority labels and provide a redacted export describing exactly what the paired device can derive and see.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Public derivation lets a separate checkout device receive and observe while signing remains with merchant; prove no signing key enters checkout.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Watch-only is not privacy-only: public derivation can reveal transaction history and future addresses.
claims.acceptance_test: Inspect pairing artifact and memory/storage inventory; verify receiving works while every spend action requires independent signer approval.

claims.capability: Distinguish seen, unconfirmed, confirmed, and reorged payments
claims.merchant_outcome: Staff make fulfillment decisions using an honest, current payment state.
claims.trigger: Wallet or node observes a transaction
claims.behavior: Show amount, transaction identity, mempool/confirmation depth, observation time, and any conflict or reorganization; do not equate first-seen with settled.
claims.preconditions: Reliable chain/mempool observation source with freshness status.
claims.qualifiers: Mempool policy is not consensus and differs across nodes; plan defines confirmation/reorg fixture requirement, not a final depth policy.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: After reorg, reverse paid/fulfillment eligibility as appropriate, retain audit history, and reconcile replacement transaction.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Tie fulfillment threshold to explicit merchant policy and show evidence/freshness rather than a generic paid badge.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: On-chain settlement provides independently verifiable public confirmation, while confirmation delay and reorg exposure require merchant policy.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Merchant bears latency and confirmation-risk choices; no single confirmation count is universally safe.
claims.acceptance_test: Simulate unseen, unconfirmed, confirmed, conflicting, and reorged transaction observations; ensure no stale state authorizes duplicate fulfillment.

claims.capability: Handle payment after request expiry or cancellation
claims.merchant_outcome: A late payment remains visible and correctly associated without silently reopening a canceled sale.
claims.behavior: Track each request address and sale after expiry; label late, canceled, partial, or unpaid distinctly and route refund/fulfillment decision to policy.
claims.preconditions: Address history and sale state persist.
claims.qualifiers: Existing product plan explicitly requires late-address tracking; no automatic refund or forced fulfillment is assumed.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: Restart, restore, or wallet migration must preserve expired request mappings and late observations.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Provide a durable exception queue with originating sale, received amount, and owner decision path.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Merchant-controlled on-chain request records support independent late-payment reconciliation; prove with a restored ledger.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: On-chain transfers cannot be canceled by checkout; late funds may require a separately authorized refund transaction and fee.
claims.acceptance_test: Pay an expired address after restart; verify it is flagged to its original sale, not treated as a new current sale, and requires explicit disposition.

claims.capability: Account for partial and excess payments
claims.merchant_outcome: Tender totals and balance due remain correct when customer pays in multiple transfers or sends too much.
claims.trigger: One or more payments observed for request
claims.behavior: Accumulate received value by request, preserve each transaction, and present remaining due or excess amount without silently changing basket value.
claims.preconditions: Exact satoshi arithmetic and durable idempotent observations.
claims.qualifiers: Payment URI amount is an instruction to wallet, not an enforcement mechanism; transactions can differ from requested amount.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: Deduplicate replayed observations and recover partial state after interruption.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Make received, remaining, and excess values explicit in ledger and receipt, with owner-controlled resolution.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Bitcoin permits objectively measured on-chain value; the merchant workflow must handle amount variance without a central processor.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Multiple transactions can add confirmation latency and UTXO fragmentation; excess funds create refund/credit policy and fee considerations.
claims.acceptance_test: Test underpayment, exact payment, overpayment, duplicate observation, and interrupted multi-transaction payment with exact satoshi reconciliation.

claims.capability: Understand future spend cost of received outputs
claims.merchant_outcome: Merchant can tell when a small output may be uneconomic to spend later.
claims.trigger: Receive output is recorded or spending is planned
claims.behavior: Show output value and estimated future spend cost range with assumptions and a threshold advisory; do not autonomously select, consolidate, or spend coins.
claims.preconditions: UTXO-level data and fee assumptions available.
claims.qualifiers: Standalone plan says advisory only; no coin-selection authority or hard loss guarantee.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: Recalculate advisory when fee conditions change; preserve received funds even if currently uneconomic.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Attach an explainable sat/vB and input-size estimate to each UTXO and state that it is advisory.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Direct merchant receipt enables control over when outputs are combined/spent, with transparent cost consequences.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: UTXO privacy and fee optimization can conflict; consolidation itself costs fees and links activity.
claims.acceptance_test: Use controlled UTXO values and fee scenarios; advisory accurately estimates spend cost range and never creates/broadcasts a transaction.

claims.capability: Approve fee and destination before spend
claims.merchant_outcome: Merchant controls whether and when a transaction is signed and what fee is paid.
claims.trigger: Withdrawal, sweep, or refund is proposed
claims.behavior: Display destination, amount, selected inputs, fee rate/absolute fee, confirmation estimate and replacement policy; require owner approval on trusted signer display.
claims.preconditions: Current signing mode and approved authority flow remain in force.
claims.qualifiers: No signing change is approved; RPC fee options are a comparator for choice, not a proposal to automate.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: Handle fee bump failure or stale inputs by returning to explicit review, never by changing destination or amount silently.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Offer an advisory review that makes fee and output tradeoffs understandable before existing owner approval.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Merchant-held keys avoid a third-party spending authorization gate; proof is transaction signing only after local owner approval.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Self-authority entails fee management and safeguarding; replacement can change a transaction before confirmation.
claims.acceptance_test: Review and sign a test spend; compare displayed destination, amount, inputs, fee, and actual transaction; verify no unsigned proposal can spend.

claims.capability: Interoperate payment requests through URI and QR
claims.merchant_outcome: Customer wallet can scan a standards-based request with amount and sale context.
claims.behavior: Encode a Bitcoin payment URI with exact amount and appropriately bounded label/message; render QR and retain plain address/manual fallback.
claims.preconditions: Supported address/script type and receiving wallet compatibility.
claims.qualifiers: BIP321 is current URI proposal; QR scanning behavior varies by wallet/app; no compatibility is claimed without a test matrix.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: If scan fails, show validated address and amount separately; prevent staff from editing address unnoticed.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Show interoperable request plus an address-only/manual route and validate the actual wallet on target devices.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Bitcoin URI/QR supports direct wallet-to-merchant payment without processor checkout integration; prove scan-and-pay across named wallets.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: URI fields can expose sale metadata to wallet or screenshots; QR is a transport format and does not ensure payment.
claims.acceptance_test: Scan requests with specified wallets/devices; compare decoded network, address, amount and optional metadata, including malformed URI rejection.

claims.capability: Offer NFC handoff of payment request URI
claims.merchant_outcome: Customer can tap a supported terminal to receive the payment request without camera use.
claims.behavior: Expose the same validated payment URI via a standard NFC NDEF URI record and keep QR/manual fallback.
claims.preconditions: Terminal and phone support compatible NFC data exchange and app URI handling.
claims.qualifiers: NFC format source does not prove payment-app launch or Bitcoin wallet support; per-device interoperability is unknown.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: Failed read or wrong app must leave sale unchanged and allow QR/manual route.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Prototype against named merchant/customer phones only after device support is established; log no customer identifier.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: A standard URI carrier can reduce checkout friction while avoiding provider-controlled payment credentials; prove successful transfer into compatible wallet.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: NFC availability and URI routing vary by device/OS; tap can reveal request context to nearby device.
claims.acceptance_test: On each target phone, tap and inspect decoded URI, then test fallback and ensure repeated taps do not duplicate or mutate a sale.

claims.capability: Limit unnecessary disclosure during payment
claims.merchant_outcome: The customer and merchant avoid publishing avoidable identifying details in payment instructions or transaction metadata.
claims.behavior: Use one-time addresses; keep customer details and sale metadata local by default; warn before exposing transaction disclosure exports.
claims.preconditions: Local records and privacy-limited export controls.
claims.qualifiers: Public blockchain transactions are observable; BIP321 labels/messages are client-side request fields, not confidential fields.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: If receipt or export is shared, disclose fields and scope; preserve local records without publishing sales history.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Minimize external metadata and give merchants per-export disclosure preview.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Direct settlement can avoid a payment processor receiving sales data, but blockchain visibility and address linkage remain.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Public transaction graph analysis can expose relationships; address rotation is not anonymity.
claims.acceptance_test: Inspect generated URI, QR, receipt, logs, and exports to confirm no unintended PII; document unavoidable public chain data.

claims.capability: Delegate checkout without spending authority
claims.merchant_outcome: Staff can accept and observe payments without changing wallet authority or spending funds.
claims.behavior: Grant request creation and payment status only; reserve authority changes, signing, refunds/spend, and recovery artifacts to owner-approved capabilities.
claims.preconditions: Identity/permission controls exist and are enforced at durable API boundary.
claims.qualifiers: Product plan requires role separation; exact staff authorization implementation is not established by protocol sources.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: Revoke staff access and confirm offline/restored device cannot continue using stale authority beyond documented expiry.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Separate public receive data from signing access and report what a role can observe or change.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Public derivation can support limited receiving roles without spending keys; prove least privilege with adversarial role checks.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Staff may still see customer/payment data; local key separation does not solve device compromise or account misuse.
claims.acceptance_test: Cashier can issue request and observe state but cannot export secret material, change destination, sign, or alter owner configuration.

claims.capability: Recover on-chain receipt and authority after device loss
claims.merchant_outcome: Merchant can restore keys or independently recover funds and still reconcile all issued/late addresses.
claims.behavior: Document and rehearse recovery from merchant-held backup; include public address derivation and issued-request ledger recovery separately from private keys.
claims.preconditions: Backup artifact is current, usable, and held by merchant.
claims.qualifiers: Key backup and sales-history backup are different; seed ownership alone does not restore application records.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: Restore on clean hardware and reconcile derived addresses, UTXOs, and old issued addresses before retiring old device.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Provide a recovery checklist and independently verifiable backup freshness/coverage indicator.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Independent key recovery can avoid a vendor account being necessary to regain authority; prove offline restore.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Merchant bears backup secrecy, physical security, and operational testing; backup exposure increases theft risk.
claims.acceptance_test: Conduct clean-device recovery using merchant-held artifacts; verify spend authority and identify every issued address mapped to open/late sales.

claims.capability: Know inbound liquidity before promising Lightning acceptance
claims.merchant_outcome: Cashier only offers Lightning when funds can actually be routed to the merchant.
claims.behavior: Assess channel direction, inbound capacity, confirmed/funded status, peer availability and current conditions before offering; never infer inbound capacity from wallet key ownership or total channel balance.
claims.preconditions: Running node with current channel and route information.
claims.qualifiers: Plan requires confirmed capacity/funding/availability gates; not a guarantee of route or payment success.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: When capacity becomes insufficient, stop offering Lightning and route customer to on-chain/cash choice without losing sale state.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Expose readiness as current evidence and freshness with reason unavailable, not a guaranteed capacity badge.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Merchant-operated node can control its receive availability directly; proof requires successful measured receiving under merchant-owned operational control.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Inbound capacity is finite, directional, may require capital/provider action, and can change; no free or prepaid liquidity assumption.
claims.acceptance_test: Vary inbound capacity, funding confirmation, peer connectivity, and stale status; checkout offers Lightning only when declared policy gates pass.

claims.capability: See capital and on-chain costs before funding channels
claims.merchant_outcome: Merchant understands channel opening/funding cost and the opportunity cost of locked funds.
claims.behavior: Show funding amount, on-chain fee estimate, confirmation condition, capital committed, usable inbound/outbound direction, and any provider fee separately.
claims.preconditions: Node exposes channel state and fee quote.
claims.qualifiers: Protocol requires on-chain channel funding; fees and provider terms are not fixed by protocol. No prepaid/free liquidity claim.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: If funding remains unconfirmed, canceled, or reorged, do not report usable capacity; explain recovery path.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Provide a readiness/funding breakdown and distinguish funds committed from capacity usable for incoming payments.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Direct node control may reduce dependence on hosted invoice services but requires explicit capital and chain-fee spending.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Funds are tied up in channel state; opening and closing add chain fees and operational overhead.
claims.acceptance_test: For a channel lifecycle, reconcile requested funding, transaction confirmation, usable directional balance, fees, and reorg/failure behavior.

claims.capability: Account for Lightning receiving fees and route failures
claims.merchant_outcome: Merchant knows whether a payment completed and what network or liquidity constraints affected attempts.
claims.behavior: Track invoice amount, payment status, received amount, and applicable route/forwarding or service fees; expose failed versus pending versus settled distinctly.
claims.preconditions: Node reports payment lifecycle and invoice identity.
claims.qualifiers: BOLT routing fees are peer-advertised and route outcomes are dynamic; exact merchant fee incidence depends on route and arrangement.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: On timeout/outage, reconcile payment hash/status before issuing another invoice or changing tender.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Show invoice expiry, status, and failure reason where available; require reconciliation before retry on ambiguous status.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Bitcoin Lightning can support direct wallet payments but route availability and fees remain part of operating economics.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: A route failure does not imply customer did not pay until status is reconciled; fees and success are not guaranteed.
claims.acceptance_test: Test paid, rejected, expired, pending, and unknown attempts with repeated customer retries; ensure one completed sale and accurate fees.

claims.capability: Support or clearly reject multipart Lightning payments
claims.merchant_outcome: Customer can pay a merchant invoice split across routes without ambiguous partial settlement.
claims.trigger: Invoice generated and wallet attempts payment
claims.behavior: Declare MPP support only when receiver and invoice features actually support it; track all parts under one payment and fulfill only on final settled status.
claims.preconditions: Node implementation supports chosen MPP behavior; customer wallet supports it.
claims.qualifiers: BOLT invoice feature support and MPP behavior are protocol/version dependent; library selection alone is not proof.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: After partial parts or node restart, recover aggregate status and avoid treating individual unresolved HTLCs as settled revenue.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Include MPP interoperability in named-wallet acceptance matrix; otherwise surface unsupported status and usable fallback.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Open protocol invoicing may interoperate across wallets when required features overlap; prove with multiple implementations and partial failure.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: MPP can leave unresolved parts and increases state/recovery complexity; must not imply any wallet can pay any invoice.
claims.acceptance_test: Exercise multi-part completion, one-part failure, timeout, duplicate parts, restart, and invoice expiry across named sender and receiver versions.

claims.capability: Show Lightning outage without losing checkout truth
claims.merchant_outcome: Merchant can continue checkout with other tenders when the node, peer, or network is unavailable.
claims.behavior: Disable or clearly mark Lightning with reason and last-seen time; preserve sale and offer supported alternatives.
claims.preconditions: Checkout separates sale state from Lightning node availability.
claims.qualifiers: Plan says cash and card availability must not change Bitcoin truth; Lightning is separate receiving mode.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: After node returns, reconcile existing invoices/payments before opening new tender attempts or marking a sale unpaid.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Provide deterministic fallback and recovery state for stale node connection and ambiguous invoice outcome.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: A merchant-owned node avoids mandatory hosted payment account reliance, while requiring local uptime and network connectivity.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Node must remain operational and reachable enough for protocol duties; outages can delay or strand operational state.
claims.acceptance_test: Disconnect node before and during payment; verify fallback, restart reconciliation, and no duplicate fulfillment across all attempts.

claims.capability: Preserve channel state safely across backup and restore
claims.merchant_outcome: Merchant does not mistake a key backup for a complete live Lightning node recovery.
claims.trigger: Backup, device migration, restore, or crash
claims.behavior: Track freshness and consistency of channel manager/monitor state; stop Lightning if required state is stale or missing; explain that seed/key possession alone may not restore current channels.
claims.preconditions: Implementation provides safe persistence and monitor synchronization.
claims.qualifiers: LDK 0.2.8 docs and BOLT protocol identify integrator state duties; LND static backup is an implementation-specific recovery comparator.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: Use tested implementation recovery procedure; stale state can risk channel funds, and static channel backup may force closure rather than restore live channel state.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Expose backup health and recovery mode separately from key custody; gate Lightning offers on validated freshness and integrity.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Merchant-owned keys support independent control but do not make Lightning channel state independent of peers or persistence.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Channel state requires careful consistency; recovery can require peers, force close, on-chain fees, and delayed access.
claims.acceptance_test: Inject stale/missing manager and monitor backups; verify Lightning stays disabled until safe recovery, then reconcile balances and close outcomes.

claims.capability: Exit a Lightning provider or node without provider permission
claims.merchant_outcome: Merchant can withdraw from a provider arrangement and recover merchant funds through protocol-defined exit paths.
claims.trigger: Provider relationship ends, node migration, or provider unavailable
claims.behavior: Document channel ownership, peer/provider role, key material, backup artifacts, close procedure, required on-chain fees, timelocks, and dependency on peer response; test unilateral exit.
claims.preconditions: Merchant has applicable channel keys and required current state.
claims.qualifiers: Key ownership is not identical to channel-state independence; unilateral exit may not be immediate and may depend on valid state and chain access.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: If provider does not cooperate, use documented unilateral close and sweep path; track timelocks and fee bump needs.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Present exit as tested procedure with time/cost estimates and identify any peer/service dependency.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Self-operated channel keys can reduce provider permission dependence; validate unilateral recovery without provider approval.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: No guarantee of immediate liquidity; force close requires on-chain fee and waiting periods, and state loss can be serious.
claims.acceptance_test: In isolated test channel, remove provider cooperation and recover using merchant-controlled current state; measure time, fees, and inaccessible interval.

claims.capability: Know who operates the receiving node
claims.merchant_outcome: Merchant can identify whether funds and protocol state are operated locally or by a hosted service.
claims.behavior: Name node operator, key holder, channel funder, backup operator, service dependencies, and what the provider can observe or control.
claims.preconditions: Deployment architecture and provider terms are known.
claims.qualifiers: Plan accepts merchant-controlled authority; no mandatory custody or permission for recovery. Hosted provider capability claims require provider-specific verification.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: If provider is removed, merchant knows exact migration/closure and recovery process.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Show authority map at setup and in status screen, with unresolved provider dependencies labelled.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Local node operation may reduce third-party operational dependence, but must prove in actual deployment and recovery.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Running a node shifts uptime, upgrades, backups, network exposure, and channel liquidity operations to merchant.
claims.acceptance_test: For each deployment mode, map signing authority, channel state storage, funding ownership, provider permissions and exit test results.

claims.capability: Understand how inbound capacity is acquired and paid for
claims.merchant_outcome: Merchant can choose a sustainable way to receive without being told liquidity is free or guaranteed.
claims.behavior: Explain available paths such as counterparty channel, swap/service, or organic channel flows only when actually supported; disclose funding, service fee, timing, counterparty and privacy tradeoffs.
claims.preconditions: A specific path and provider or counterparty are selected and separately validated.
claims.qualifiers: No provider availability, pricing, uptime, or compatibility inferred; no pre-paid/free liquidity claim.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: If acquisition fails, preserve sale and offer on-chain/cash alternative; do not charge merchant without confirmed terms and approval.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Provide options only after verifying exact current provider terms and show what each changes in authority and liquidity.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Open protocols can permit multiple liquidity approaches without a single mandatory provider; proof requires measured cost, terms, and exit.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Acquiring inbound capacity may require capital, an on-chain transaction, provider fee, counterparty risk, and operational coordination.
claims.acceptance_test: Compare documented options using actual quoted fee, confirmed usable inbound amount, time to readiness, authority map, and exit outcome.

claims.capability: Interoperate Lightning invoice display with customer wallets
claims.merchant_outcome: Customer wallet can read a valid network-specific invoice and merchant can reconcile payment by invoice identity.
claims.behavior: Present QR-compatible invoice with correct network and amount; show expiry and fallback; never treat QR scan as payment.
claims.preconditions: Invoice is generated by active receiving node and compatible wallet.
claims.qualifiers: BOLT 11 documents encoding; wallet compatibility and current offer formats vary; no test coverage claimed.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: On app-switch failure or expiry, regenerate only after checking whether existing invoice was paid.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Test named wallets and show invoice network/amount/expiry in cashier flow.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Standard invoice encoding supports wallet interoperability without processor-specific checkout account; prove with target wallet tests.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Invoice validity expires and QR is not proof of payment; long/complex codes and app handling vary.
claims.acceptance_test: Scan invoice using named supported wallets on target devices and test wrong-network, expiry, amount mismatch, and duplicate scan cases.

claims.capability: Safely handle unknown required URI parameters
claims.merchant_outcome: Merchant and customer do not make a payment when the wallet cannot honor a required instruction.
claims.behavior: Treat unknown required (`req-`) parameters as unsupported and reject the entire request; ignore only optional unknown fields as permitted by the standard.
claims.preconditions: Wallet implementation conforms to URI standard and displays the resulting request for customer authorization.
claims.qualifiers: BIP 321 defines required extension handling; compatibility still varies by wallet.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: If rejected, preserve sale and allow staff to issue a supported plain request only after validating the same amount and address.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Validate URI construction and expose unsupported-wallet recovery without weakening required instructions.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Standards-based payment requests can interoperate while safely failing closed on required features; prove against multiple wallets.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Unknown optional data can be safely ignored per standard; unknown required parameters must not be silently discarded.
claims.acceptance_test: Create URIs with supported, unknown optional, and unknown `req-` fields; named clients must honor or reject as specified, with no payment on reject.

claims.capability: Prevent wrong-network payment requests
claims.merchant_outcome: Customer is not directed to a test or alternate network address for a mainnet sale.
claims.behavior: Bind request to configured Bitcoin network; validate address/URI network markers before display and refuse mismatched network data.
claims.preconditions: Network is explicitly configured and address parser recognizes supported address formats.
claims.qualifiers: BIP 321 specifies network indications for certain address forms; wallet behavior must be tested.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: Network mismatch leaves sale unpaid and requires regenerating the request from configured merchant wallet.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Show network in cashier and customer wallet review, and block cross-network request construction.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Merchant-controlled receiving supports a direct, verifiable network destination; prove mismatch rejection before payment.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Some address encodings do not expose a simple text prefix; compatibility and network labeling must be correct.
claims.acceptance_test: Attempt mainnet sale with testnet/signet URI/address and wrong `tb` parameter; block or reject each mismatched request.

claims.capability: Validate refund destination and amount separately
claims.merchant_outcome: Customer receives a refund only to a destination they explicitly provided and confirmed for that refund.
claims.trigger: Refund requested for an on-chain sale
claims.behavior: Collect a fresh destination per refund, validate its network and script support, show exact amount and fee, and require explicit approval before signing.
claims.preconditions: Original sale and refund liability are recorded; existing owner signing authority remains unchanged.
claims.qualifiers: Bitcoin URI standard does not establish merchant refund protocol; this is a workflow requirement inferred from merchant-controlled outbound payment risks. Never treat a prior receive address or customer identity as proof of refund destination.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: If address is invalid, wrong-network, changed, or unconfirmed by customer, do not sign; retain refund as owed/pending.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Provide a two-person/owner review surface for destination, amount, network, and fee before existing signer approval.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Direct merchant-controlled refund transactions avoid processor permission but require destination verification and explicit fee control.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: A valid address does not prove recipient identity; irreversible misdirection and fee expense remain merchant risks.
claims.acceptance_test: Refund to fresh test destinations on matching and mismatching networks; alter address between request and approval and ensure signed payload requires renewed review.

claims.capability: Set a merchant-approved fee budget for outgoing transactions
claims.merchant_outcome: Merchant understands and limits the fee exposure for payouts, refunds, and sweeps.
claims.behavior: Show estimated absolute fee, rate, confirmation target and configured maximum budget; refuse automatic signing above budget and allow explicit owner override through existing path.
claims.preconditions: Wallet exposes fee estimate and transaction size/inputs; threshold is configured by owner.
claims.qualifiers: Bitcoin Core exposes fee-rate and confirmation-target options; fee estimates are software and network dependent.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: If fee estimate unavailable or exceeds budget, hold transaction for review and preserve the unpaid/refund-owed status.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Translate fee-rate choices into total merchant cost with a clear budget and fallback.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Merchant-controlled spending allows a locally chosen fee ceiling instead of a provider-defined price; measure overspend avoidance.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: A low cap may delay settlement; a high cap may overpay; fee estimate is not confirmation guarantee.
claims.acceptance_test: Test transaction size, fee rates, unavailable estimator, budget boundary and override; verify actual fee never exceeds approved amount without renewed authorization.

claims.capability: Prevent concurrent spends from selecting the same UTXO
claims.merchant_outcome: Refund and payout operations do not race, double-reserve funds, or fail after staff believe they were approved.
claims.trigger: Multiple outgoing transactions are prepared concurrently
claims.behavior: Reserve selected UTXOs before authorization; present conflicts and release reservation only on cancel, expiry, or confirmed broadcast outcome.
claims.preconditions: Wallet supports input locking or equivalent durable transaction coordination.
claims.qualifiers: Bitcoin Core RPC offers optional UTXO locking; implementation-specific behavior must be verified.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: After crash, reconcile wallet locks and transaction mempool/chain state before retry or reuse.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Make reservation state durable and visible across registers while keeping signing authorization owner-controlled.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Local wallet coordination can avoid external spending approval while preventing conflicting attempts; prove under interruption.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Input reservation can temporarily reduce available balance; stale locks need safe expiry/reconciliation.
claims.acceptance_test: Run two concurrent refund/spend preparations against the same UTXO; assert only one reserves it, and crash/restart reconciles lock state without duplicate broadcast.

claims.capability: Retain monitoring for every issued address through late-payment resolution
claims.merchant_outcome: A late or delayed payment is discoverable after request expiry, staff shift change, app restart, and wallet recovery.
claims.trigger: Payment request expires, sale closes, or merchant changes wallet device
claims.behavior: Keep a durable issued-address index and monitor it through an explicit retention/closure policy; display last scan height/time and unresolved late status.
claims.preconditions: Wallet/node rescan capability or trusted sync source and durable mapping exist.
claims.qualifiers: BIP32 supports derivation, not a monitoring guarantee; merchant tracking is required by existing plan.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: After device loss or a long offline interval, rescan from safe height and reconcile late payments before declaring request closed.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Expose monitoring freshness, covered range, and unresolved old requests in closeout/recovery.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Merchant-held address derivation enables independent monitoring after provider exit; test by rescan after offline period.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Long retention costs storage/sync and creates durable transaction history; no finite expiry erases on-chain transfer possibility.
claims.acceptance_test: Issue then expire request, take device offline, restore on clean device and rescan; verify any late transfer links to correct original sale and freshness is explicit.

claims.capability: Understand unilateral exit dependencies and delayed funds
claims.merchant_outcome: Merchant knows what must remain available to force close and when funds can be swept.
claims.trigger: Lightning peer/provider unavailable or cooperative close fails
claims.behavior: Document need for current channel state/monitor, chain observation/broadcast, fee handling, output scripts, and applicable on-chain delay; report force-close and sweep stages separately.
claims.preconditions: Node has valid channel state and keys; chain access and fee strategy are available.
claims.qualifiers: BOLT 3 describes delayed local outputs; BOLT 5 on-chain handling; LDK maintains manager/monitor separation. Availability of peers/watchtowers changes operational resilience, not channel state independence.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: Lost/stale backup, unavailable peer, reorg, or fee spike can delay exit; follow supported safe recovery procedure and keep funds status unresolved until sweepable.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Expose verified recovery prerequisites and estimated wait/cost from actual channel terms; do not promise immediate exit.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Merchant keys can permit unilateral protocol exit without provider permission, provided current state and on-chain mechanisms are available.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Unilateral closure is slower and may cost more than cooperative close; state, chain fee, timelock, and counterparty/watchtower conditions matter.
claims.acceptance_test: In isolated channel fixture, disable cooperation, restore from documented state, publish valid unilateral close, process delay/reorg, sweep outputs, and record elapsed blocks and fees.

claims.capability: Limit payment request metadata that can identify payer or sale
claims.merchant_outcome: A payment request does not unnecessarily reveal a customer name or sensitive sale details.
claims.behavior: Use minimum required amount and merchant reference; do not encode customer name, personal identifier, or detailed basket in publicly visible labels/message unless explicitly needed and disclosed.
claims.preconditions: Payment request supports optional fields and merchant has a local sale mapping.
claims.qualifiers: BIP 321 labels/messages are request fields, not a confidential channel; payment itself remains publicly observable on-chain.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: If a request is copied/shared, retain only intended metadata; regenerate request if exposed details are sensitive and policy allows.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Default to opaque local reference and preview all fields before generating QR/NFC.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Direct wallet requests can avoid forwarding customer identity to a payment platform, but public ledger data persists.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Metadata minimization does not prevent payer address linkage or network observer inference.
claims.acceptance_test: Inspect QR/NFC payload for identifying fields and test screenshots/logs; verify default URI contains no PII and local receipt still resolves sale.

claims.capability: Avoid address reuse and transaction linkage across sales
claims.merchant_outcome: Repeated sales are less trivially associated through the same merchant receive address.
claims.behavior: Issue distinct receiving addresses and consider address reuse when planning spends; make any reuse explicit with privacy impact.
claims.preconditions: Wallet derives fresh receive addresses and records them durably.
claims.qualifiers: Core wallet source documents avoid_reuse option as a privacy measure; address uniqueness does not anonymize public transactions.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: If derivation state is restored, ensure next index and prior mapping do not roll back into address reuse.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Warn before reusing address and maintain deterministic derivation-index recovery.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Self-controlled derivation can support fresh addresses without provider account creation; prove address uniqueness through backup restore.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Fresh addresses complicate accounting and public history still permits clustering; privacy can conflict with consolidation/input selection.
claims.acceptance_test: Generate requests across restart and restore, prove no duplicate address issuance, then exercise explicit reuse override with warning.

limitations: Protocol documentation specifies formats and mechanisms but does not show the target merchant’s wallet, device, node, account, region, or staff workflow works.
No competitor capability comparison is performed; this bundle does not claim POS parity.
Bitcoin Core mempool rules and fee estimates are policy/software/version-dependent; confirmations and reorg exposure require an explicit merchant policy.
No wallet vendor or hardware manual was selected as a product comparator; device-specific pairing, QR and NFC interoperability remain unverified.
Lightning route availability, inbound liquidity, fees, provider terms, channel funding, backup freshness, peer behavior, unilateral exit time, and recovery cost were not measured.
LDK 0.2.8 and LND docs are narrow implementation references, not evidence of OpenBMT’s selected or deployed Lightning implementation.
No claim asserts a new technology or feature is implemented. Merchant improvements and acceptance tests are hypotheses/criteria only.

Further product decisions are required for confirmation/fulfillment threshold, privacy disclosure policy, stale node thresholds, supported wallets/devices, MPP support, and Lightning deployment ownership.
URI payment standards do not define a merchant refund workflow; fresh refund destination confirmation is a merchant safety requirement requiring product-specific acceptance evidence.
NFC format source was reviewed, but target phone/app interoperability is unknown pending tests.
Bitcoin Core wallet RPC/source is a narrow comparator for fee options, UTXO locking, and avoid-reuse behavior; it does not establish OpenBMT behavior.
LDK 0.2.8 source was inspected from the locally cached published crate matching Cargo.lock; its remote docs page was not verified during this research.
